title: Module D — Genie Retrieval Result
description: Output of the Recruitment Genie layer for one raw JD. Contains the JD interpretation, the SQL Genie generated, and the retrieved repository-level evidence rows. Per the retrieval instructions, Genie retrieves and never scores — this schema has no candidate score or rank field, and additionalProperties:false keeps it that way.

genie_space_id.description: Databricks Genie space the query ran against.

jd_text_hash.description: Hash of the raw JD, so a repeated submission is recognisable and cacheable.

interpreted_requirements.description: How Genie read the JD's requirement language. The team wrote no JD parser — this is the semantic layer's work.

mapped_skills.description: Audit trail from JD wording to canonical skill, e.g. 'containerized deployment' -> Docker via the synonym vocabulary.

generated_sql.description: The query Genie actually produced. Stored verbatim so a judge can see the retrieval was dynamic, not hardcoded.

evidence_rows.description: One row per (candidate, repository, skill). Multiple repositories demonstrating the same skill are all preserved — collapsing them is Module C's job.

confidence.description: Read straight from REPOSITORY_SKILL.confidence — the deterministic Evidence Score. Genie passes it through untouched and must never treat it as a candidate score.

registered_student_ids.description: Candidates in scope for this job. Lets Module C detect a candidate who was registered but returned zero evidence rows, rather than silently dropping them from the ranking.

warnings.description: e.g. a JD term that mapped to no canonical skill — a signal to extend the synonym vocabulary.
